systems.name: Mind change selection
systems.description: Selection, arrangement, execution, and revision of changes to a model, a person, their interaction, or the conditions in which they think and act.
systems.scope: Mind change includes changes of time, duration, pace, order, location, environment, bodily readiness, attention, perception, representation, knowledge, uncertainty, trust, emotion, motivation, goals, priorities, identity, memory, skill, available possibilities, decision rules, action, relationships, tools, resources, and the way later changes are selected. These overlap and do not exhaust the possibilities. Distinguish a person's state, a model's working state, and their shared conditions wherever different operations or evidence follow. For a model, changes to context, retrieved material, representation, instructions, tools, and working assumptions are available only through the host's actual capabilities; a conversation does not establish a change to model weights.

standards.name: Beneficial direction
standards.requirement: Ground improvement in the person's expressed or contextually supported concerns, the relevant facts, and the consequences. Understanding, experience, exploration, and capability can matter without producing immediate action. Keep inferred purposes revisable. Agreement, intensity, novelty, confidence, activity, and satisfaction do not alone establish benefit.

standards.name: Choice of what changes
standards.requirement: Choose the recipient, locus, direction, extent, duration, and conditions of the change as well as the technique. Preserve a useful state when changing it would add cost or damage. More dimensions changed is not automatically better. An unfamiliar starting point can be explored before the problem or destination is settled.

standards.name: Open selection
standards.requirement: The current interpretation, problem, criteria, method inventory, medium, and selector remain open to revision. A method earns its place through the operation it can perform here. Neither catalog membership nor a keyword match settles relevance. Missing evidence of benefit can justify a bounded informative trial; it is not evidence of no benefit.

standards.name: Whole arrangement
standards.requirement: Judge operations together when one enables, obstructs, or changes another. Preserve required prerequisites and result-dependent branches. Include effects on later opportunities and on the ability to recognize, choose, perform, and revise future changes. Do not claim broad transfer without identifying the uses that could change.

standards.name: Total cost
standards.requirement: Count model work, user attention, reading, interruption, choice, execution effort, delay, opportunity cost, switching, recovery, and maintenance when consequential. Compare with the strongest available ordinary response and, where informative, waiting or leaving matters unchanged. A fast trivial gain need not beat a slower consequential gain. Do not invent a universal score or numerical weights.

standards.name: Agency and factual integrity
standards.requirement: Keep the person able to inspect, disagree, decline, and redirect. Do not manufacture agreement through deception, concealed pressure, or dependency, or change their priorities merely to make the intervention look successful. Reconsidering a goal or value is allowed; its benefit needs a basis beyond increased compliance. The same standard applies when the model's own selection criteria change.

standards.name: Observed effect
standards.requirement: Separate a proposed mechanism, a predicted effect, a performed attempt, and an observed consequence. Use evidence suited to the change: self-report can establish reported experience; a task can reveal a distinction or capability; actual conduct can show uptake. None automatically establishes the others. Model agreement with itself is not independent confirmation.

standards.name: Time and context
standards.requirement: Allow benefit to appear, decay, reverse, or transfer over time and across settings. Compare against what would change anyway. Immediate ease does not settle later usefulness, and durability is required only when the intended use requires it. Prefer evidence obtainable through the ongoing work before adding assessment burdens.

standards.name: Correction and continuity
standards.requirement: A correction must alter an applicable later choice or operation. Preserve the conditions, scope, evidence, and trigger for reuse, including a case where the correction should not apply. Store durable records through available mechanisms when authorized and useful; do not assume future retrieval merely because a record exists.

standards.name: Selection overhead
standards.requirement: Apply these obligations in proportion to the live choice. Reuse settled context and criteria. A clear low-cost answer can be delivered directly. Extra diagnosis, comparison, measurement, or construction of another selector needs a plausible contribution larger than its burden. Unknown effects remain unknown; procedural compliance does not certify a universal maximum.

steps: Recover the current request, relevant prior corrections, available material, and actual capabilities. Identify what is observed, inferred, or unavailable about the person, model, and setting. Retrieve resolvable context yourself. Ask for a fact only when its answer would materially change the next contribution and cannot reasonably be recovered; do not make the person choose your method or complete an intake form.

Anticipate the strongest response or continuation you would presently choose. Identify the interpretation and selection rule that make it appear appropriate. At a consequential unresolved choice, construct a credible alternative that changes what is being changed, not just its wording. If the governing interpretation excludes a promising direction, temporarily set its continuation aside and examine that direction without first pretending the original is false. Skip manufactured alternatives when no consequential choice remains.

Locate a useful next change using the scope and standards. Inspect whether the obstacle is in the model's interpretation or conduct, the person's current state or access, or their conditions of interaction. Keep competing locations when evidence does not distinguish them. If the needed change is unclear, choose an observation, encounter, or reversible exploratory operation that could reveal it; diagnosis and a fixed destination are not prerequisites for exploration.

Retrieve an existing operation when its actual input, transformation, and result fit the situation. Read the exact source before claiming to execute a named original procedure. Adapt or construct an operation when the available ones leave a consequential gap, keeping the adaptation distinct. Consider a different representation, timing, setting, tool, role, or allocation of work when these could change what becomes possible. A capability or authorization gap changes what can be performed now.

Construct the viable arrangement. For each consequential operation, identify what it consumes, what changes, what later operation uses that change, and what result would redirect the sequence. Compare meaningful orderings when they can differ. Include preparation, a pause, repetition, simplification, removal, or stopping when warranted. A prerequisite may earn its cost through a later operation even when it has little immediate visible effect.

Select using the supported benefits, competing consequences, and total costs over the relevant horizon. Eliminate a route when another is at least as good on every supported relevant comparison and better on one, with no unresolved material trade-off. Otherwise preserve the trade-off and choose on the best supported current priorities. Where uncertainty would reverse the choice, obtain a discriminating observation if its likely value warrants the cost; otherwise make a bounded reversible choice and retain the uncertainty. Do not turn estimates into measurements.

Perform the selected change through available, authorized means. Revise the model's working interpretation, representation, search, context, or operation before addressing a problem caused there. Construct the representation, inspect the source, provide the useful distinction, or carry out the task when that is the contribution. Describe a human action when the person must perform it. A proposed relocation or later encounter is not a completed change; a later action requires an actual scheduling or continuation mechanism.

Compare the consequence with the expected change and the relevant alternative using the least burdensome adequate evidence. Check consequential effects on other dimensions, including future revisability. Keep natural change, changed criteria, new resources, and other competing explanations visible when attributing an effect. If a criterion itself changes, preserve the earlier comparison and justify the revised criterion separately. A worked model example establishes only what happened in that example.

Use the result to continue, alter the operation or order, change the locus, revisit the concern or criterion, obtain missing evidence, or stop. A rejection reopens the model of the situation; it does not automatically call for stronger rhetoric or repeating the same method. Stop when the requested work is sufficiently handled or the next supported marginal benefit no longer warrants the burden; defer when the opportunity is genuinely better later and a feasible continuation exists.

Retain only the reusable situation, operation, observed consequence, scope, and future trigger needed for subsequent use. Propagate corrections to the rule and dependent work that produced the failure. Check the next suitable recurrence and a boundary case when available. Present the contribution in the form the person can use, with material reasons or uncertainty; keep method-selection bookkeeping out of the response unless it helps their decision or they request it.

Use the present model to perform these operations when it has the required capacity. If a different available system would materially improve the work, give it these standards, the concrete situation and source material, relevant corrections, known constraints, available operations, and the next decision it must resolve. Require the operation or contribution and its material basis, allow revision of a mistaken target or arrangement, and integrate the actual result. Handoff cost competes with doing the work directly; creating another selector is not an obligatory recursive step.
systems.standing: Operational instruction standard with worked design cases; comparative human benefit and universal optimality are unestablished.
systems.source: User request, 2026-09-08: automate selection and arrangement for beneficial efficient mind change across time, location, representation, motivation, and all other aspects; develops the current Subject Systems construction operations and Reasoningtool2 contribution-selection contract.

systems.name: Design alternative construction
systems.description: Development of possibilities that differ in their available consequences, with useful alternatives retained during exploration.
steps: Generate candidates under different assumptions, forms, or constraints relevant to the live work. Identify what each candidate makes possible.
Group candidates only where their differences do not change the intended inquiry or use. Keep a surprising difference visible even when no final application is known.
Select several directions for the distinct possibilities they expose. Preserve the reason for retaining each rather than assigning a universal novelty score.
For each retained direction, vary the assumption that produced it and develop its consequences. Cross selected features when their combination could create a new possibility.
Compare the resulting possibilities with their parents. Reject a claim of novelty when only the words changed; preserve useful recombination without falsely claiming independent invention.
Return the developed alternatives, the distinctions among them, and the direction each makes worth pursuing next.
systems.standing: specified design, version 0.1. Prospective effectiveness is unestablished.

systems.name: Design candidate exploration
systems.description: Construction of an artifact through comparisons that develop its form and requirements.
steps: Produce materially different forms of the artifact at the fidelity needed for the choice. Include an alternative that changes the assumed form where that could alter the result.
Present or exercise the candidates in the relevant context. Record whole-candidate selections separately from comments about a particular aspect.
Generate variations that preserve the favored aspect while changing another consequential property. Include a contrast that could show the favored aspect was incidental.
Derive candidate requirements from the selections and stated use. Preserve their evidence and the distinction between a necessary condition and one attractive implementation.
Assess the factual constraints of the candidate through the appropriate inspection or test. Approval and buildability receive separate results.
Revise the design when feasibility changes; revise the requirement when the changed design exposes a mistaken interpretation. Preserve both histories.
Return the selected or still-competing design, justified requirements, construction dependencies, and the next authorized realization step.
systems.standing: specified design, version 0.1. Prospective effectiveness is unestablished.

systems.name: Improvement candidate revision
systems.description: Revision of an object against a specified baseline, with the intended improvement and its costs preserved in the comparison.
steps: Retain the baseline and the specific respect in which improvement is sought. Preserve uncertainty about the standard if discovering it is part of the work.
Generate candidates that change a plausible cause of the limitation, including a different approach when local polishing preserves the limitation.
Use selections to identify promising changes, recording why they are favored. Do not relabel approval as measured benefit.
Compare candidate and baseline using evidence appropriate to the target: a derivation, actual use, observation, or a scoped test. Keep material context differences visible.
Determine what became better, what became worse or more costly, and which result remains unresolved. Do not hide a tradeoff in a single unsupported score.
If the criterion changes, reconsider the baseline and candidate under the revised standard. If only a proxy improves, reopen the claimed benefit.
Retain the chosen change with the actual comparison and the conditions under which another use is warranted.
systems.standing: specified design, version 0.1. Prospective effectiveness is unestablished.

systems.name: Goal achievement assessment
systems.description: Achievement under declared required conditions, with optional observations and activity state retained separately.
steps: Accept a nonempty map of required conditions, an optional-condition map, and a Boolean abandonment flag. Each observation must be true, false, or unknown. Reject an empty or malformed required map.
If any required condition is false, return not achieved and retain all failed and unknown conditions.
Otherwise, if any required condition is unknown, return undetermined with those conditions.
Otherwise return achieved. Preserve optional observations and abandonment state in every result.
When applying the result to an actual goal, examine the justification of the required conditions and the evidence for the observations.
systems.standing: Custom v0.1; executable and exercised across 54 specified condition combinations.

systems.name: Goal discovery
systems.description: Development of a goal and its achievement conditions from competing possible aims.
steps: Construct materially different candidate aims from the live situation, including different purposes and a candidate that revises the initial framing. Preserve already explicit commitments rather than pretending they are unknown.
For each candidate, construct a concrete case in which it would be met and a case that appears to meet it while missing the intended purpose.
Use existing explicit selections or obtain the particular missing comparison when needed. Separate the selected aim, the attractive consequence, and the means through which it was presented.
Change a means while preserving the proposed end, then change the end while preserving the means. Use the contrast to develop competing accounts of what mattered.
Derive candidate achievement conditions from the supported account. Keep desired properties of an artifact separate from the purpose the artifact serves.
If no candidate expresses the purpose, regenerate the aims or change the representation. If the conflict concerns what is worth pursuing, retain that conflict instead of forcing a score.
Return the current goal, grounds for it, conditions of achievement, alternatives still live, and the next decision those conditions affect.
systems.standing: specified design, version 0.1. Prospective effectiveness is unestablished.

systems.name: Criterion discovery
systems.description: Development and revision of a judgment standard through consequential differences between cases.
steps: State what kind of judgment is being developed: for example preference, validity of inference, fitness for use, or contribution to a purpose. Preserve unresolved disagreement over that target.
Collect the cases that distinguish the live proposed standards, including a case where an initially plausible standard gives a problematic verdict.
Generate alternative standards that account for the contrast. Derive what each would require in a different case before accepting it.
Separate an observed verdict from its justification. A user judgment can establish what the user chose; a claim of validity requires its own grounds.
Apply the candidate standards to the contrasting cases. Keep a contextual rule or an unresolved conflict where a single rule would erase a consequential difference.
Revise the standard or its scope and reopen the verdicts that depended on it. Leave unaffected factual claims and independent grounds intact.
Return the criterion, the comparison that motivates it, its grounds and scope, and the verdicts requiring reconsideration.
systems.standing: specified design, version 0.1. Prospective effectiveness is unestablished.

systems.name: Preference discovery
systems.description: Discrimination between accounts of a contextual preference through contrasts among selected features.
steps: Record the actual candidate, judgment, and context. Keep an explicit statement of preference separate from an explanation inferred from a selection.
Construct competing accounts of the judgment that predict a different selection somewhere. If the accounts do not yet differ on any comparison, develop the missing distinction.
Construct candidates that separate those predictions while holding other consequential features stable where possible. If they cannot be held stable, record the ambiguity the comparison leaves.
Use the actual answer. A tie, rejection of both, context-dependent answer, or inability to choose remains a possible observation; no answer is invented for the person.
Revise the accounts that disagree with the observation. A changed context may require a conditional account rather than a declaration that the person is inconsistent.
Test whether a favored feature remains favored when placed in another candidate, or whether its value depended on the whole example.
Return explicit preferences, supported conditional hypotheses, competing explanations, and the next comparison that would distinguish what remains.
systems.standing: specified design, version 0.1. Prospective effectiveness is unestablished.

systems.name: Preference question route
systems.description: Selection and continuation of a preference inquiry through the distinctions made by its possible answers.
steps: Start from a consequential unresolved distinction in the preference account. Construct alternative questions if the current wording presupposes the disputed preference.

For each candidate question, construct plausible answer branches, including neither, both, tie, context-dependent, and unable-to-judge where relevant. These are anticipated possibilities, not observations.
Derive which hypothesis or contextual distinction each answer would change. Replace a question whose answers all leave the live distinction unchanged.
Choose a question for the distinction needed by the receiving task. Use an already recorded answer when it actually addresses that question; otherwise seek only the necessary missing judgment.
After an actual answer, follow the corresponding clarification, opposition, concretization, or other justified route. Preserve alternatives that the answer did not distinguish.
Revise the question when its assumptions were rejected. Return a new discriminator or a contextual account that is sufficient for the receiving use.
systems.standing: specified design, version 0.1. Prospective effectiveness is unestablished.

systems.name: Discovery contribution assessment
systems.description: Identification of an investigation's established contribution and the further work it enables.
steps: Recover the initial inquiry and its current formulation. Record which goal, question, scope, or criterion changed and the result that warranted the change.
Separate artifacts produced from findings established. For each proposed finding, attach the supporting observation, derivation, or source at the required scope.
Compare the finding with the actual unresolved question. Record whether it resolves that scope, changes the question, exposes another alternative, or leaves the inquiry open.
Identify the next inquiry or method that can use the finding and preserve the conditions it needs. A merely mentioned relation is not a required dependency.
If work stopped for lack of access or resources, retain the needed condition without marking the question answered. If a criterion changed, reopen dependent closure claims.
Continue from the newly available work, including a new purpose made possible by success. Do not require the entire subject to be finished before using a scoped finding.
systems.standing: specified design, version 0.1. Prospective effectiveness is unestablished.

systems.name: Expression contribution construction
systems.description: Construction of text through the changes in understanding its successive contributions produce.
steps: Determine the contribution required by the actual request and available context. Keep an unresolved purpose open where writing itself is needed to discover it.
Separate the substantive material from claims still requiring a derivation, source, comparison, or other operation. Perform the needed intellectual work instead of covering the gap with explanation.

Identify what each prospective part would make the reader able to distinguish, infer, consider, or reconsider. Delete or change a part that merely announces the topic without serving the contribution.
Construct an ordering from the actual dependencies among those changes. Develop another ordering or frame if the first hides a consequential relation.
Write the passage and inspect whether it performs the intended operation. A declared intention to persuade, explain, or analyze does not count as the operation being performed.
If a premise, interpretation, or criterion changes, revise the dependent passages and preserve independently justified material.
Return the organized text at the requested scope, with evidence and uncertainty where needed for the reader to assess it.
systems.standing: specified design, version 0.1. Prospective effectiveness is unestablished.

systems.name: Reasoning approach selection
systems.description: Selection of an available reasoning approach through the contribution needed in a naming or scope problem.
steps: Identify the distinction the task must settle using the current definitions and a concrete case.
Compare the completion conditions of candidate approaches. Where apparent synonyms conceal different matters, construct a case that separates them.
Inspect an actual candidate output or a separating case. Retain the approaches that can supply the required contribution and identify any missing operation.
Choose an available approach supported by the comparison. If none supplies the contribution, construct an approach or revise the task formulation before selecting.
Execute the selected approach when required by the task and inspect its actual contribution.
Revise dependent definitions and uses while retaining stable identity, aliases, and any change of scope.
systems.standing: Custom specification v0.1, executed on one catalog naming case; general effectiveness unestablished.

systems.name: Reasoning candidate finite generation
systems.description: Every assignment in an explicitly supplied finite Cartesian product.
steps: Accept an ordered map of named dimensions to finite lists of distinct strings. Validate the names and values.
Multiply the dimension sizes. Return an input error if the product exceeds 4096.
Enumerate every tuple in dimension and value order and retain its named coordinates. An empty dimension yields no tuples; an empty dimension map yields one empty assignment.
Return the assignments. Apply any feasibility or exclusion conditions in a separate examination that retains their reasons and unresolved cases.
systems.standing: Custom v0.1; executable and used to supply cases to the achievement-assessment study.

systems.name: Claim inference finite validity
systems.description: Classical Boolean entailment of a supplied conclusion by supplied premises across their complete finite valuation space.
steps: Accept at most 12 distinct atoms, a premise list, and a conclusion. Permit Boolean constants, declared atoms, unary not, and binary and, or, implies, and iff, with nesting at most 64.
Reject malformed formulas, undeclared atoms, and exceeded bounds before issuing a verdict.
Enumerate every Boolean assignment. Evaluate the premises under each assignment; where all are true, evaluate the conclusion and retain assignments where it is false.
Return all counterexamples, the valuation count, and validity within the supplied model. Report vacuous validity when no assignment satisfies the premises.
Examine the translation from the original claim separately whenever the formal result is used to judge that claim.
systems.standing: Custom v0.1; executable and exercised on six fixed analytical inferences, with scope and input failures recorded.

systems.name: Claim inference counterexample search
systems.description: Examination of an exact inference through support paths and cases that satisfy its premises while defeating its conclusion.
steps: State the inference with its quantifiers, conditions, and intended interpretation. Separate a conclusion about truth from a recommendation or preference before selecting a challenge.
Reconstruct the particular transition on which the conclusion depends. Preserve any assumption introduced by the reconstruction as an assumption rather than a supplied premise.

Develop a challenge targeted to that transition: a case where the premises hold and the conclusion fails, a shifted definition, or an unlicensed assumption. Identify which of these the challenge actually is.
Determine whether the challenge meets its own conditions. A possibility compatible with the conclusion, an undesirable consequence, or a changed question is not automatically a refutation.
If a transition is defeated, withdraw the inference it supplied and inspect the uses that depended on it. Keep independently supported conclusions and unchallenged alternatives separate.
If no defeating case is obtained, retain the actual search scope and unresolved result. Do not infer general validity from survival of the attempted challenges.
systems.standing: specified design, version 0.1. Prospective effectiveness is unestablished.

systems.name: Problem formulation comparison
systems.description: Comparison of competing causes and repairs for a rejected result, including defects in the process that reproduces it.
steps: Recover a rejected item, the requested correction, and the content that must survive it. Keep the user's correction distinct from an inferred general rule.
Construct competing explanations of the failure. Each explanation names a condition whose removal would change the observed result.
Apply the proposed repair to a small actual specimen. Inspect which original requirements remain unsatisfied and which new defects appear.
Follow any recurring defect backward to the source record, construction decision, generator, or acceptance rule that reproduces it.
Select the formulation that accounts for the consequential failures being addressed. Retain additional causes when one repair leaves an independently produced defect.
Reopen the formulation when a result contradicts its predicted effect.
systems.standing: Specified construction system; repository applications recorded in cases/repository-construction.json.
systems.source: Repository construction design, adopted by the user on 2026-09-08.

systems.name: Content placement
systems.description: Conversion of conversational material into current subject content with its meaning, status, and dependencies preserved.
steps: Split the material at changes of subject, assertion, operation, condition, evidence, or status. Preserve dependencies between the resulting pieces.

Identify the matter each piece concerns. Recover whether it is a user requirement, a proposed account, an established result, an operation, a rejected formulation, or context needed to interpret another piece.

Compare the matter with existing definitions. Reuse an identity when the matters coincide. Refine or separate identities when one description contains several determinations. Preserve an unresolved relation as unresolved.
Place each current definition once. Connect findings, operations, applications, and evidence to that definition through the relation they actually bear to it.
Construct the reading order from the required distinctions and dependencies. Inspect whether neighboring placement implies an unsupported equivalence or containment.
Remove source-history prose from the ordinary entry when the reader can interpret and use the content without it. Preserve the source and correspondence needed to recover or revise the result.
systems.standing: Specified construction system; repository applications recorded in cases/repository-construction.json.
systems.source: Repository construction design, adopted by the user on 2026-09-08.

systems.name: Perspective consequence comparison
systems.description: Construction and comparison of perspectives through the differences they make to the same piece of work.
steps: Fix an actual piece of work and recover its governing requirements. Leave the problem formulation revisable.

Express the current perspective through what it treats as the object, relevant differences, available operations, acceptable results, and grounds for stopping. Infer these from the artifact and conduct where possible.

Change one consequential commitment: the object being organized, the unit of content, the comparison standard, the assumed reader task, the timescale of success, or a restriction on available operations.
Construct the resulting alternative on the same piece of work. Preserve the required content so that unrelated improvements do not conceal the effect of the perspective change.
Compare the alternatives by the distinctions they preserve, the work they enable, the errors they expose, and the burdens they impose.

When two cases are treated alike but require different continuations, introduce the missing distinction. When two named perspectives make no relevant difference in the stated use, treat them as equivalent for that comparison.
Examine exclusions. A reason for withholding reliance on a perspective may still permit exploration of it. A failure in one application does not by itself justify exclusion everywhere.
Combine perspectives only after assigning each contribution a role. Inspect whether one contribution's assumptions or visible expression obstruct another.
Change the problem, criterion, construction operation, or dependency when the comparison reveals a defect there. Preserve the identity of earlier comparisons when their basis changes.
Retain a useful transition with the conditions that made it useful. Check whether it affects the next applicable construction.
systems.standing: Specified construction system; repository applications recorded in cases/repository-construction.json.
systems.source: Repository construction design, adopted by the user on 2026-09-08.

systems.name: System description examination
systems.description: Identification and repair of consequential operations left unspecified by a system description.
steps: Select a concrete input and the result the system must distinguish or produce.
Execute the described operations with that input. Mark the first place where proceeding requires inventing an operation, choosing an unsupported criterion, or interpreting an undefined condition.
Construct two realizations consistent with the description that differ on the required property. If both fit, the description is insufficient for that property.
Supply the missing transformation, interpretation rule, or condition. If it must be performed by a model or a person, state the actual examination they perform and what can correct it.
Inspect result consumers. Preserve distinctions such as false, unknown, unavailable, contradictory, and inapplicable wherever they require different actions.
Remove components that supply no necessary result, evidence, condition, or useful continuation in the defined use. Retain construction, exploration, and verification steps whose value appears later.
Exercise a case that defeated the earlier design. Record the actual difference in result or continuation.
systems.standing: Specified construction system; repository applications recorded in cases/repository-construction.json.
systems.source: Repository construction design, adopted by the user on 2026-09-08.

systems.name: Expression construction
systems.description: Direct expression of a subject or operation with the distinctions required for its use.
steps: Establish what the reader needs to identify, distinguish, infer, or perform from this entry. Use the accepted task and the content's actual dependencies.
Draft the substantive description or operation directly. Use the subject or system name when a heading is needed to distinguish entries.
Locate every condition that changes the claim or action. Place it with the proposition or operation it qualifies.

Remove a sentence or label provisionally. Compare the resulting interpretations and available actions with the original. Retain it when its removal loses a required distinction, creates a consequential ambiguity, or prevents the intended use.
Compare the remaining form with the source and intended content. Repair semantic drift caused by compression, including altered scope, modality, authority, or unresolved status.
Read the result without its construction notes. Inspect whether its sequence, naming, grouping, and level of detail express the intended priorities.
Challenge the apparent simplicity. Check whether the reader now has to invent a missing condition, retrieve a basic distinction from several files, or interpret a compressed slogan.
systems.standing: Specified construction system; repository applications recorded in cases/repository-construction.json.
systems.source: Repository construction design, adopted by the user on 2026-09-08.

systems.name: Correction propagation
systems.description: Revision of a producing rule and its dependent outputs, followed by examination of uptake and scope.
steps: Preserve the rejected result, the correction, and the relevant setting.
Construct a nearby case to which the correction should apply and another in which applying it would damage the result. Use the contrast to establish its scope.

Identify the producing decision or mechanism. Distinguish an incorrect source fact, a mistaken selection rule, a faulty transformation, an expression habit, and an acceptance rule that failed to catch the result.
Revise the responsible source or rule. Find its dependent current outputs through existing references, generation paths, and targeted content search.
Regenerate or revise affected outputs. Preserve independent content and the evidence needed to recover previous states.
Apply the changed construction rule to the nearby case. Check for the original failure in altered wording or placement.
Apply the scope boundary case. Repair the rule if it removes necessary content or constrains unrelated work.
Treat a stored correction as effective only when it changes an applicable later result.
systems.standing: Specified construction system; repository applications recorded in cases/repository-construction.json.
